question: Who wrote ‘The Story of My Experiments with Truth’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi:**

 
 
• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi (1869-1948) wrote "The Story of My Experiments with Truth," his autobiography.
 
• The book chronicles his life from his childhood to his political activism in South Africa and India.
 
• It details his personal philosophy and his commitment to truth, nonviolence, and self-reliance.
 
• Gandhi's autobiography is considered a significant work of 20th-century literature.
 
• He wrote this book in gujarati, and it was translated into many languages.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale:**

 
 
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (1866-1915) was a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress and a social reformer.
 
• He was known for his moderate political views and his emphasis on education and social reform.
 
• He served as a mentor to Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He was a very important political figure during the indian independence movement.
 
• He founded the Servants of India Society.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:**
 
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru (1889-1964) was India's first Prime Minister and a key figure in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He wrote several books, including "The Discovery of India" and "Glimpses of World History."
 
• His writings reflected his socialist views and his vision for a modern, secular India.
 
• He played a very important role in the formation of the modern Indian nation.
 
• He was a very influential political leader.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:**
 
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856-1920) was a prominent Indian nationalist, teacher, and independence activist.
 
• He was known for his radical views and his slogan "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it!"
 
• He was a strong advocate for Indian self-rule.
 
• He published the newspapers Kesari, and Mahratta.
 
• He was a key figure in the early indian independence movement.
